title: Change the owner of a file or directory
summary: Use chown to change who owns a file or folder. You usually need administrator rights (sudo) to change the owner to another user.

steps.explain: Run chown with sudo to change the owner of the specified file or directory to the target user.

placeholders.name: USER
placeholders.description: The username of the new owner

placeholders.name: FILE_OR_DIRECTORY
placeholders.description: Path to the file or directory

rollback.explain: To undo, change the owner back to the original user. You need to know the previous owner.

placeholders.name: FILE_OR_DIRECTORY
placeholders.description: Path to the file or directory

warnings: Changing ownership incorrectly can prevent you or other users from accessing files.
You typically need sudo privileges to change the owner to a different user.
